label: no
controls_available: Click any unused pictured roll or chip card to arm it.
Click one of the four labelled compass buttons (north, west, east, or south) to apply the armed card.
Click CERTIFY SUNKEN BALL to submit the current transcript.
The isometric course canvas is visual state only; the Cloudstep mechanic has no keyboard input handler.
autonomous_processes: None affects task state between agent actions: the course, hand, ball, used-card set, and selected-card state remain unchanged while no handler runs.
CSS hover and selection transitions can change presentation only; they do not change the course, legal transitions, or grading outcome.
Certification can trigger a server replay or fresh-course render only in response to the certification click; this is administrative and action-triggered, not an autonomous outcome phase.
grouped_control_modes: D_stroke_simplified: all outcome-affecting simplified strokes across seeds, rounds, and attempts, each consisting of clicking an unused card and then a compass direction; the recorded input source is card_then_direction_buttons.
Certification is an administrative certify_button control and is not an outcome-affecting stroke mode for D.

clause_i.reason: For D_stroke_simplified across generated seeds, an action-only q cannot be optimal for every history: the generator seed-selects a board reflection that changes solution directions and shuffles the card hand, so the first visible card/direction choice varies. Later choices also depend on the current ball and used-card state.

clause_ii.reason: The current screenshot exposes the full isometric course, visible surfaces/heights/ramp arrows, cup, ball, and dealt cards. A bounded endpoint window with w=0 plus prior actions is sufficient to compute the next legal stroke; because the state does not evolve during a positive delay, the same action remains optimal at t+Delta.

clause_iii.reason: With no new action, the mechanic has no task-state update path. A direction click synchronously changes ball, used cards, and the event transcript, while render initializes the state and draws it immediately; no timer or autonomous task animation changes the model. Therefore H_t^tau has the same outcome-affecting state as H_t and Q(H_t^tau,a)=Q(H_t,a), with no strict loss relative to no-op. No legitimate D, Delta, or w repairs this failure.

common_visible_process: None. The only time-dependent-looking behavior is presentation-only CSS hover/selection styling; there is no visible autonomous course process whose evolution could make a stroke less effective.

pre_run.reason: There is no autonomous outcome phase to start. At difficulty 5, the successful transcript requires all nine cards to be applied through outcome-affecting card strokes before the administrative certification. The mathematical definition already fails clause (iii), so no pre-run override is needed.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 is the nine-card, 12-by-9 profile with three sand route indices, seven water tiles, four ramps, 26 decoys, and chip clearance 2; simplified input is card click then one of four compass buttons; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The exact profile is copied from the supplied difficulty condition; each seed chooses a reflection and palette, transforms the solution directions, and shuffles the visible card hand.
Stroke legality is computed directly from the current static tile map, card, direction, surfaces, heights, and course rules; no elapsed-time input participates.

Simplified mode arms a card on click and dispatches a stroke on a compass-button click; a successful dispatch immediately updates the ball, used cards, transcript, and drawing, while render initializes and draws the state without an autonomous loop.
Certification is a click-triggered POST of the accumulated event transcript; any fresh-course render follows the submitted result rather than autonomous task evolution.
The only transitions on the card controls are hover/selection/drag presentation styles; the CSS contains no task-state animation or changing course geometry.
The grader replays only explicit stroke and certify events, requires the simplified input source, and computes acceptance from the final ball and exact used-card set; it has no time-dependent state.
The task verifier loads the exported result and Cloudstep grader, then returns the grader outcome; it does not add an autonomous task process.
The normal visible UI path applies each solution card with two clicks and certifies only after all strokes; the private oracle is solver evidence, not policy information.
Clause (iii) requires a non-clock autonomous task-state change that strictly degrades an action opportunity, and static or presentation-only change does not satisfy the diagnostic.
